title: Align on minimum compatibility matrix and pinning exemptions for community model entries
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket formalizes the minimum metadata contract and compatibility guidance required to onboard community/open models into Redwood's model catalog, with a new lightweight "pin-exempt" pathway for experimental variants. The goal is to reduce ambiguity during intake, prevent runtime regressions for customers, and enable fast but safe onboarding for community-provided weights.

Context and motivation:
We routinely receive community model submissions with incomplete runtime compatibility details (e.g., quantization support, KV-cache semantics, max context length). Without a consistent minimum contract, engineers spend significant time discovering runtime incompatibilities during model verification, delaying catalog availability. Existing pinning guidance is fragmented across PRDs and onboarding docs; we need a single, developer-friendly contract that: 1) defines minimal metadata fields; 2) defines acceptance tests and runtime checks; 3) introduces a managed "pin-exempt" label for variants that can ship to the catalog with guarded visibility (experimental / preview) and explicit runtime disclaimers.

Scope (what this ticket will deliver):
- A machine-readable minimum metadata contract for community model entries (fields listed below).
- A human-readable onboarding checklist for PM/Eng/SE reviewers.
- Acceptance criteria and end-to-end verification steps (automated tests where feasible).
- A "pin-exempt" policy describing when a variant may be allowed without a formal pin and the required mitigations (visibility, audit log, fallback variant).
- UX copy that will appear in the catalog entry summarizing compatibility (for Console/Docs).

Out of scope:
- Changes to runtime enforcement (ENG work item). This ticket defines the contract; ENG tickets will implement validators and runtime fallbacks.
- Enterprise-only catalog rules (handled by a separate Private-catalog initiative).

Minimum metadata contract (required fields for onboarding):
- model_id (string): canonical catalog identifier
- semantic_version (string): suggested version tag from upstream (not runtime pin)
- min_runtime_version (string): minimum Redwood runtime release necessary to serve the model safely (e.g., "runtime-1.18")
- max_context_tokens (string): declared max context length (e.g., "8192")
- kv_cache_compatible (string): "true" | "false" (does model require/benefit from KV cache semantics)
- quantization_support (string): comma-delimited list of supported quant profiles (e.g., "8bit,4bit-ntq")
- hardware_recommendation (string): preferred HW class (e.g., "A10G/4xA100")
- fallback_variants (string): comma-delimited list of catalog variant IDs to use if this variant fails at runtime
- inference_behaviour_notes (string): short freeform note listing known behavior differences (e.g., missing tokenizer, nonstandard logits ordering)
- provenance_link (string): link to upstream weights/license and model card
- compatibility_notes (string): one-line summary for Console display (automatically generated if left blank)

Pin-exempt policy (summary):
- Purpose: allow rapid preview of early or experimental variants while protecting production workloads.
- Eligibility: model variants that pass automated safety and licensing checks but fail one of the non-critical compatibility checks (e.g., quant profile missing but CPU fallback possible).
- Required mitigations for pin-exempt variants:
  - Explicit Console flag: "experimental - not pinned" visible to customers
  - Default routing: only accessible to users with opt-in in Console and to internal test API keys
  - Fallback: must specify at least one fallback_variant that is pinned and production-ready
  - Audit: onboarding reviewer must add a "pin_exempt_rationale" note and select a time window for re-evaluation (max 90 days)
